items.followUp: What are the three components of an ATP molecule?

rubric.why: Award for identifying the nitrogenous base and sugar that form adenosine.
rubric.how: Check that the answer identifies adenine and ribose, or names their combined unit, adenosine.

rubric.description: States that ATP has three phosphate groups.
rubric.how: Check for the number three or the term triphosphate linked to phosphate.

modelAnswer: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) consists of adenine, a ribose sugar and three phosphate groups.

items.followUp: Define macronutrients and give two examples.

rubric.why: The defining feature of micronutrients is that organisms need them in very small amounts.
rubric.description: States that micronutrients are required in very small amounts.
rubric.how: Check for an expression that conveys a very small required quantity.

rubric.why: Examples show understanding of the kinds of nutrients classed as micronutrients.
rubric.how: Check for at least two valid examples, such as vitamins and minerals or iron and zinc.

modelAnswer: Micronutrients are nutrients required by the body in very small amounts.

items.followUp: Name the blood component that contains iron and state its function.

rubric.why: Iron is an essential component of hemoglobin in red blood cells.
rubric.description: States that iron is used to form hemoglobin.
rubric.how: Check that the answer links iron with hemoglobin.

rubric.why: Hemoglobin transports oxygen, explaining an important role of iron in the body.
rubric.description: States that iron helps transport oxygen in the blood.
rubric.how: Check for an explicit link between iron/hemoglobin and oxygen transport.

modelAnswer: Iron is needed to make hemoglobin in red blood cells.
Hemoglobin carries oxygen from the lungs to the body tissues.

items.followUp: State two functions of the small intestine.

rubric.why: The large intestine absorbs water and salts from the undigested material.
rubric.description: States that the large intestine absorbs water and salts.
rubric.how: Check for absorption of water and/or salts.

rubric.why: The large intestine forms and stores faeces before elimination.
rubric.description: States that it forms or stores faeces.
rubric.how: Check for formation or storage of faeces.

modelAnswer: The large intestine absorbs water and salts from undigested food.
It forms and stores faeces before their removal from the body.

items.followUp: Write two symptoms of peptic ulcer.

rubric.why: Pain or a burning sensation in the abdomen is a common ulcer symptom.
rubric.how: Check for pain or a burning sensation in the stomach or abdomen.

rubric.why: These are recognised symptoms associated with ulcers.
rubric.how: Check for at least one valid symptom, such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion or loss of appetite.

modelAnswer: A person with an ulcer may have pain or a burning sensation in the abdomen.
Other symptoms may include nausea, vomiting or indigestion.

items.followUp: Explain how evaporation from leaves produces transpiration pull.

rubric.why: Water loss from leaf surfaces initiates the pull.
rubric.description: States that evaporation or water loss occurs from the leaves.
rubric.how: Check for evaporation or water loss from leaves.

rubric.why: Evaporation creates tension/suction, which is transmitted through the cohesive, continuous column of water in the xylem.
rubric.description: Explains the resulting tension/suction or how it is transmitted through the water column.
rubric.how: Check for tension, negative pressure, suction, or cohesion maintaining a continuous water column.

modelAnswer: Evaporation of water from the leaf surfaces creates tension or suction in the leaves.
Cohesion between water molecules keeps a continuous water column in the xylem, transmitting this pull upwards.

items.followUp: Give two differences between arteries and veins.

rubric.why: The direction of blood flow distinguishes arteries from veins.
rubric.description: Contrasts the direction of blood flow in arteries and veins.
rubric.how: Check that arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry blood toward it.

rubric.why: Wall structure or the presence of valves provides a valid structural difference.
rubric.description: Gives a structural contrast between arteries and veins.
rubric.how: Check for a correct paired contrast, such as thick versus thin walls or valves in veins.

modelAnswer: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, whereas veins carry blood towards the heart.
Arteries have thick, elastic walls; veins have thinner walls and valves.

items.followUp: Name one Muslim scientist who contributed to biology and describe his contribution.

rubric.why: Biology is defined by its subject: life and living organisms.
rubric.description: Defines biology as the study of life or living organisms.
rubric.how: Check that the definition identifies life or living organisms as the subject of biology.

rubric.why: Bu Ali Sina made an important contribution to medicine through his medical writings.
rubric.description: Names Bu Ali Sina and his contribution to medicine or Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb.
rubric.how: Check for the scientist's name together with medicine or his medical work.

rubric.why: Abdul Malik Asmai studied and wrote about animals.
rubric.description: Names Abdul Malik Asmai and his work on animals.
rubric.how: Check for his name together with animals or a valid animal group he wrote about.

rubric.why: Ibn al-Nafis is credited with describing pulmonary circulation.
rubric.description: Names Ibn al-Nafis and his description of pulmonary circulation.
rubric.how: Check for his name together with pulmonary or lung circulation.

modelAnswer: Biology is the study of life and living organisms.
Bu Ali Sina wrote Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb, an important medical work.
Abdul Malik Asmai wrote about animals, including horses and camels.
